findings.description: MONEY ENCODING IS CODE-ONLY. Spec says only 'consumed as pure values'. Code pins an exact display encoding via `fmt_cents`: `format!("{sign}{}.{:02}", a/100, a%100)` over `Cents.0` — sign prefix `-` iff negative, fixed two decimals from integer cents, NO thousands separator, NO currency symbol — emitted as `Cell::Value(String)` (written as a Sheets `userEnteredValue`, so it parses as a number). tests/formula.rs re-implements that exact formatter and asserts each of the five columns equals it, plus literal `"50.00"` / `"20.00"` for the Federal-2022 row. All 3 B runs reconstructed the rule to the digit (B1 §006, B2 §3, B3 §006); no A run could — all three deferred formatting to an invented `Cell::money(Cents)` / `CellValue::Money(Cents)` typed cell carrying raw integer cents, i.e. the spec forced them to leave the encoding open.

NEVER-BLANK INVARIANT, AND ITS ASYMMETRY WITH THE SIBLING BAND. Spec never says the five figures are always populated. Code renders all five unconditionally through `fmt_cents` (zero → `"0.00"`, never `""`), while the accrual band immediately above renders `Amount` as `a.applied_cents.map(fmt_cents).unwrap_or_default()` — an empty string when `None`. tests/formula.rs asserts `!row[rcol(name)].text().is_empty()` for all five, with the comment '(the gap the review flagged)', i.e. it is a defended, previously-violated invariant. All 3 B runs raised it as an explicit unwanted-behavior clause (B1 §007, B2 §5, B3 §007). Nothing in SHEET-TAB-005 distinguishes the two bands' blank semantics.

'PER (Jurisdiction, Tax Year)' READS AS KEYED; CODE IS ONE-ROW-PER-SUPPLIED-ELEMENT IN INPUT ORDER. Spec text: 'populate the band per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year)'. Code: `for r in annual_rows { reserve_rows.push(...) }` over a plain `&[AnnualRow]` — no keying, no uniqueness check, no dedupe, no sort; row order is exactly the caller's slice order and a duplicated `(jurisdiction, tax_year)` pair would double-render the band. A-side (all 3) independently read the spec as key-addressed and imposed determinism the code lacks: A1/A2 funnel through `BTreeMap<(&Jurisdiction, TaxYear), &AnnualReport>` with last-writer-wins on duplicates, A3 takes a `BTreeMap<(Jurisdiction, TaxYear), AnnualReport>` as the parameter type outright; all three flagged 'ordering unspecified by the EARS — I impose sort so republished tabs diff cleanly'. B-side (all 3) pinned the mirror image as a requirement: 'exactly one row per supplied `AnnualRow`, in the supplied order, row count == `annual_rows.len()`' (B1 §003, B2 §3, B3 §003) — and the test asserts `tax.reserve_summary.rows.len() == annual.len()` and zips positionally. Neither key uniqueness nor a stable republish ordering is stated anywhere in the spec; both are load-bearing for an idempotently republished tab.

BAND IDENTITY AND PLACEMENT ARE ENTIRELY CODE-SIDE. Spec names the band and nothing more. Code pins: `TAX_RESERVE_TAB: &str = "Tax · Reserve Summary"`; the band is a *separate* `ViewTab` returned inside `TaxView { accruals, reserve_summary }`, with its own frozen header, distinct from the accrual band named `TAX_TAB = "Tax"`; it is deliberately NOT a fifth entry in `VIEW_TABS: [&str; 4] = [Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax]` and does not appear in `workbook_tab_order()`; and the stated invariant is that neither band ever carries among-data summary / blank / label / embedded-header rows so both stay natively filterable. All 3 B runs led with this (B1 §001, B2 §1, B3 §001+§010). Corroborating evidence that the spec omits it: A1 and A2, reading the spec alone, both invented a `Row::note("No tax reserve activity")` label row — precisely the construct the code's design forbids.

JURISDICTION AND TAX-YEAR CELL RENDERING. Spec mentions `(Jurisdiction, Tax Year)` only as the band's grain. Code pins the exact cell text via `jurisdiction_label`: `Jurisdiction::Federal` → `"Federal"`, `Jurisdiction::State(code)` → `format!("State({code})")`; and Tax Year → `r.tax_year.0.to_string()` (bare decimal, e.g. `"2022"`, not a date). The test looks rows up by `text() == "Federal"` and `text() == "2022"`, making both the row's lookup identity. All 3 B runs pinned both rules including the `State(<code>)` wrapper (B1 §008, B2 §3, B3 §008); no A run guessed the wrapper form (A1 used an assumed `juris.as_str()`, A2/A3 `Display`).

VALUE/FORMULA BOUNDARY FOR THIS BAND IS TEST-ENFORCED BUT SPEC-SILENT. Every reserve cell is constructed as `Cell::Value`, never `Cell::Formula`; the band carries no `GOOGLEFINANCE` dependency and is kernel-exact as-of-last-sync, explicitly contrasted with the Positions tab's live estimate. `tests/formula.rs::tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula` sweeps every cell of both bands asserting `!cell.is_formula()`. SHEET-TAB-005 says nothing about the value/formula split (it may be owned by a sibling boundary spec, but this requirement does not carry it). All 3 B runs stated it as a first-class clause (B1 §005, B2 §4, B3 §005).

HEADER LITERALS AND COLUMN POSITIONS AS A CONTRACT. `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` is exactly `["Jurisdiction","Tax Year","Accrued","Moved","Paid","Outstanding","Shortfall"]`, 7 columns at indices 0–6, and the tests address columns by header name through it (`rcol`), making both the strings and their positions load-bearing. The spec does list the five figures in that same order (so figure ordering is spec-traced — all 3 A runs reproduced it exactly), but it never states that the two key fields are rendered as the two leading columns, never fixes the header strings, and never makes column position part of the contract. B1 §002 / B2 §1 / B3 §002 all pinned it verbatim.

PUBLISH-PATH CONTRACT INHERITED BY THE BAND, PLUS INFALLIBILITY. Code/doc pins: data rows written from `DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2` beneath a frozen header row 1 that is *never* rewritten on republish, as one atomic per-tab `batchUpdate` with residual-tail truncation (`SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view` contract); and `render_tax(&[Accrual], &[AnnualRow]) -> TaxView` is infallible — no `Result`, unlike `render_positions` — and needs no `Snapshot`, `AliasMap`, or marks. All 3 B runs attached this to the reserve band (B1 §010, B2 §7, B3 §011). SHEET-TAB-005 is silent on all of it; arguably owned by a sibling publish spec, which is why this ranks below the band-local findings.

EMPTY / ABSENT-FIGURE BEHAVIOR IS SPEC-OPEN, AND THE INVENTED ANSWER IS ONE THE CODE FORBIDS. The spec does not say what the band shows when `tax::annual_report` yields no rows. Forced to decide, 2 of 3 A runs emitted a header plus a `Row::note("No tax reserve activity")` placeholder row 'so the tab shape is stable' (A1 §7, A2 §7); A3 chose header-only (§'Empty input yields header only'). The code emits header + zero data rows — and its own band invariant explicitly bars label/blank rows inside the range, so the majority A answer would violate it. Listed last: the A runs split 2/1 and the behavior has no basis in the spec text, so this is weak spec-under-determination rather than a spec-traced miss.

notes:
Files read: {scratch}/audit-baseline/crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (render_tax at L707-750, TAX_RESERVE_HEADER L230-238, TAX_RESERVE_TAB L52, VIEW_TABS L70, fmt_cents L473-478, jurisdiction_label L752-757) and .../crates/sheets-view/tests/formula.rs (tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula L273-298, reserve_summary_carries_all_five_kernel_exact_columns L300-409).

WHAT IS COHERENT (no finding): the core of the requirement lands cleanly. The code performs zero arithmetic on the five figures — `fmt_cents` is presentational only, `outstanding_cents` and `shortfall_cents` are copied straight from `AnnualRow`, there is no totals row, no netting, no `accrued - paid` derivation, no cross-check between columns. All 3 A runs volunteered exactly that prohibition ('clamping would be tax math', 'deriving shortfall would be the tax math the requirement forbids') and all 3 B runs reconstructed it as an explicit no-tax-math clause. The figure set and the figure ORDER (accrued, moved, paid, outstanding, shortfall) also round-trip exactly. Negative/zero figures pass through signed and unclamped in both directions.

WHY BD-DRIFT RATHER THAN B-ONLY-DRIFT: the mass of surplus is unambiguously B-side (7 of 9 findings). But the '(Jurisdiction, Tax Year)' grain is one clean shared axis — the A runs unanimously read the phrase as key-addressed and built `BTreeMap` keying, dedupe policy, and a deterministic sort; the B runs unanimously reconstructed the opposite pin ('one row per supplied AnnualRow, in the supplied order'). Same gap, surfaced independently from both ends, so it classifies BD rather than B-only. The empty-state item is a second, weaker touchpoint in the same shape (spec silence let A invent a label row the code's band invariant forbids).

STABILITY DETAIL. A-side: high — all three produced the same 7-column single-row-per-pair projection in the spec's figure order, the same pure-pass-through prohibition, the same BTreeMap-imposed ordering with the same stated reason (clean republish diffs), the same signed/unclamped Cents handling, and the same 'no GOOGLEFINANCE cells here' call. They diverge only on the empty-state note row (2/1) and on return shape (`Band` vs `Vec<Vec<CellValue>>`) — presentation of the sketch, not behavior. B-side: high — near-identical clause sets across all three (band identity + separation from the accrual band, header literal, one-row-per-supplied-row + count equality, kernel-exact verbatim figures / no view math, Value-not-Formula, the fixed-2-decimal signed money rule with the same worked examples, never-blank, Federal/State(<code>) labels, VIEW_TABS exclusion, DATA_START_ROW=2 publish contract). No contradiction between B runs; B2/B3 additionally noted render_tax infallibility.

MINOR, NOT LISTED AS A FINDING: the spec names `tax::annual_report` as the source, but `render_tax` accepts an unvalidated `&[AnnualRow]` slice from the caller with nothing tying those rows to `annual_report`'s output, and no completeness check. That is ordinary dependency injection and is subsumed by the BD keying finding, so it is not scored separately. Also unscored: A-side field-name guesses (`accrued` vs the real `accrued_cents`), which are naming trivia rather than behavior.
